thread.title: Tech Stocks Thrashed; Nasdaq Loses Key Support Level | Investor's Business Daily

author: KEN SHREVE
title: Tech Stocks Thrashed; Nasdaq Loses Key Support Level | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Tech stocks sold off hard in the stock market today as the Nasdaq composite pierced its 50-day moving average in heavy volume. Tesla ( TSLA ), Workday ( WDAY ) and Align Technology ( ALGN ) were big decliners in the Nasdaq 100. Microsoft ( MSFT ), Home Depot ( HD ) and Nike ( NKE ) lagged in the Dow.
X With about one hour left to go in the session, the Nasdaq composite led the declines, down 2%. The Russell 2000 slumped 1.6%. The small-cap index is down 3% so far this week. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones industrial average gave back just over 1%. Another distribution day was taking shape for the Nasdaq, with volume tracking much higher than Wednesday. Volume on the NYSE was on pace to be slightly lower.
Rising rate fears fueled negative sentiment. The 10-year Treasury yield added 1 basis point to 3.19% after soaring Wednesday to its highest level since July 2011.
The bond market sold off sharply Wednesday, but money didn't exactly move into stocks. In fact, it was a stalling session for the S&P 500, where a 0.6% intraday gained faded to 0.1% by the close. Volume rose.
Tech Stocks Hammered Top-ranked industry groups in IBD's database were among the hardest hit on Thursday. The Leisure-Movies & Related group lagged due to pronounced weakness in tech stocks like Roku ( ROKU ) and Netflix ( NFLX ). Biotechs, chip equipment firms and software stocks also fell sharply. Besides Workday, big decliners in the enterprise software group included IBD Sector Leader ServiceNow ( NOW ), Paylocity ( PCTY ) and Twilio ( TWLO ).
Inside the IBD 50 , tech stocks came under intense selling pressure again. The Innovator IBD 50 ETF ( FFTY ) was down more than 3% as longtime leaders Veeva Systems ( VEEV ), Paycom Software ( PAYC ) and Grubhub ( GRUB ) fell sharply.
In stock market results today , FANG stock Amazon.com ( AMZN ) breached its 50-day moving average, falling more than 2.5%. Amazon and Apple ( AAPL ) were in the news early Thursday after a Bloomberg News report claimed the Chinese government installed spy chips into data-center servers run by Amazon and Apple. In a statement, Amazon called the Bloomberg story "untrue."
Other news wasn't all bad, though. Heavy-volume gainers included Eli Lilly ( LLY ). Shares jumped about 4% to a new high after the company announced positive trial results for its diabetes treatment.
Constellation Brands ( STZ ) gapped up on strong earnings, but the stock was well off session highs. Beer sales rose 10.5% to $1.63 billion, making up just over 70% of total sales. The company's investment in marijuana firm Canopy Growth ( CGC ) has paid off nicely.
In IPO news, Guardant Health ( GH ) had a solid debut after pricing last night at 19, above the proposed range of 15-17. Shares were recently trading around 34.25. Guardant makes noninvasive blood-based cancer diagnostic tests.
